It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing a world where “sin is the monarch that rules the heart of every man” (Romans 6:12), and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the cost of peacemaking in this hour, knowing that “all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution” (2 Timothy 3:12)? [35, 53, 584, 1351, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” because the “whole creation has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth until now” (Romans 8:22), or are you seeking the “settled certainty” that “nothing... shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord” (Romans 8:38–39)? [223, 289, 335, 339, 702, 1409, 1429, 1462, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many offer “spiritual placebos” like the “prosperity gospel,” we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs our souls by reminding us that “you were bought at a price; therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God’s” (1 Corinthians 6:20) [1, 11, 28, 486, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1503, 1670, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the violent cost of reconciliation is not an “administrative anomaly” but was “included in God’s eternal decree” according to the promise: “Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things that are not yet done, saying, ‘My counsel shall stand, and I will do all My pleasure’ ” (Isaiah 46:10) [15, 22, 68, 1143, 1391, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

### **Section 1: The Blood of the Righteous Crying Out (Abel)**

**Verse**
“And He said, ‘What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground’ ” (Genesis 4:10). [1204, 1234, 1274, 1309, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture reveals that the “record of history” begins with the “wicked deed” of the first murder, where Cain was “hostile toward God, whom he could not kill, and jealous of his brother, whom he could kill” (1 John 3:12, “not as Cain who was of the wicked one and murdered his brother”) [1203, 1233, 1248, 1274, 1284, 1285, Conversation History]. This unrighteous violence occurred because “unbelief is the seed” of the “seed of Satan” struggling against the “woman’s seed,” proving that the presence of a peacemaker often provokes the “animosity” of those whose “every intent of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually” (Genesis 6:5) [384, 1209, 1227, 1278, 1388, 1413, Conversation History]. Yet, even in death, the peacemaker’s testimony remains, for “by faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, through which he obtained witness that he was righteous... and through it he being dead still speaks” (Hebrews 11:4) [1232, 1274, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be terrified” by those who “kill the body but cannot kill the soul,” for the Lord is the “Judge of all the earth” who “will not at all acquit the wicked” (Matthew 10:28; Genesis 18:25; Nahum 1:3) [11, 227, 670, 819, 1071, 1138, 1231, 1253, 1502, Conversation History]. Recognize that “he who trusts in his own heart is a fool,” and you must instead “tremble at My word,” which promises that “precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of His saints” (Psalm 116:15; Proverbs 28:26; Isaiah 66:2) [11, 76, 709, 827, 858, 1313, 1406, 1503, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **theocratic context**, the “avenger of blood” was a “near of kin” chosen to deal with a suffers’ loss, yet even then, God provided “cities of refuge” to ensure that “the manslayer may not die until he stands before the congregation in judgment” (Numbers 35:12) [435, 1067, 1069, 1305, 1306, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our posture, showing that our “victory” is found in a Savior who “when He was reviled, did not revile in return,” for “the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh” (1 Peter 2:23; 2 Corinthians 10:4) [13, 21, 32, 43, 92, 725, 807, 811, 959, 1081, 1313, 1365, 1426, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

### **Section 2: The Rejection of Truth and False Peace (The Prophets)**

**Verse**
“ ‘They have also healed the hurt of My people slightly, saying, “Peace, peace!” When there is no peace’ ” (Jeremiah 6:14). [83, 84, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **John MacArthur**—notes that “the peace of the wicked is born of delusion,” as the religious leaders of Israel offered “spiritual placebos” that acted as a “cradle of security” on the “precipice of hell,” while God was actually “angry with the wicked every day” (Psalm 7:11) [1, 84, 85, 1394, Conversation History]. Those who spoke the “true knowledge” of God were often “massacred” because the world “did not receive the love of the truth,” as seen when Stephen rebuked his executioners: “ ‘Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those who foretold the coming of the Just One’ ” (Acts 7:52) [48, 113, 196, 1128, 1341, 1349, 1395, 1420, 1452, 1453, 1503, 1506, Conversation History]. Authentic peacemaking is “always costly” because it requires the “sword of the Spirit” to pierce “hearts of unbelief” and “cut into our pride and self-will” (Hebrews 4:12) [256, 257, 274, 349, 1351, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” for the Lord “will fight for you,” even when “the world hates you” because “you are not of the world” (Exodus 14:14; John 15:19) [82, 94, 201, 672, 804, 1197, 1211, 1408, 1410, 1515, Conversation History]. You should “not be deceived” by a “market-driven strategy” that promises “temporal happiness” by “shaving off the edges” of the truth, for “the world is passing away along with its desires, but whoever does the will of God abides forever” (1 John 2:17) [21, 28, 91, 1405, 1412, 1414, 1502, 1503, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Mosaic Economy vs. New Covenant Peace**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “national greatness” and “military skill” were often “temporal signs” of God’s favor, as seen when “five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you shall put ten thousand to flight” (Leviticus 26:8) [409, 1313, 1314, 1326, 1353, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by revealing that “My kingdom is not of this world,” and our true “repose of the soul” is found in the “spiritual house” where “everything the Sabbath signified has been completely fulfilled in the finished work of Christ” (John 18:36; Hebrews 4:10) [13, 16, 17, 21, 24, 26, 32, 38, 97, 136, 142, 440, 1023, 1113, 1203, 1313, 1315, 1320, 1326, 1329, 1426, 1431, 1445, 1524, 1529, 1636, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

### **Section 3: The Ultimate Peacemaker and the Blood of the Cross (Christ)**

**Verse**
“and through Him to reconcile all things to Himself, by Him, whether things on earth or things in heaven, having made peace through the blood of His cross” (Colossians 1:20). [333, 712, 731, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Reformed theology—echoed by **Voddie Baucham**—teaches that “Christ is the living embodiment of divine love,” and He accomplished the “greatest good ever” by being “stricken, smitten by God, and afflicted” to “bear the sins of many” (Isaiah 53:4, 12; Hebrews 9:28) [102, 133, 350, 715, 716, 1195, 1337, 1393, 1398, Conversation History]. He is the “Mighty God” and “Prince of Peace” who “fulfilled justice by His death,” for “without shedding of blood there is no remission” (Isaiah 9:6; Hebrews 9:22) [12, 13, 18, 145, 1196, 1331, 1340, 1503, Conversation History]. Because “He Himself is our peace, who has made both one,” believers can have a “Spirit-wrought confidence” that the “debt is paid” and we have been “reconciled to God through the death of His Son” (Ephesians 2:14; Romans 5:10) [38, 73, 132, 284, 443, 729, 730, 757, 1332, 1429, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Your life is not your own” because “He who did not spare His own Son, but delivered Him up for us all” has “made us His slaves” and “welcomed us into His family” (Romans 8:32; 1 Corinthians 6:19–20) [11, 12, 13, 101, 216, 217, 723, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1503, 1670, Conversation History]. You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” to find “tranquility of soul,” but instead find “repose” in His promise: “ ‘Peace I leave with you, My peace I give to you; not as the world gives do I give to you’ ” (John 14:27) [11, 24, 51, 82, 89, 123, 142, 564, 1072, 1406, 1445, 1503, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual to Reality**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “animal sacrifices” were a “shadow of things to come,” providing only “ceremonial cleansing” that “did not eliminate sin” (Colossians 2:17; Leviticus 16:30; Hebrews 10:4) [11, 13, 32, 97, 142, 360, 394, 414, 420, 603, 781, 782, 787, 1313, 1330, 1334, 1344, 1345, 1430, 1440, 1442, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our worship, revealing that “by one offering He has perfected forever those who are being sanctified,” rendering the “temple made with hands” obsolete (Hebrews 10:14; Acts 7:48) [5, 11, 13, 17, 32, 101, 107, 142, 360, 402, 464, 612, 630, 728, 790, 833, 908, 1042, 1059, 1123, 1128, 1129, 1138, 1202, 1208, 1243, 1262, 1267, 1313, 1315, 1316, 1334, 1335, 1402, 1403, 1406, 1417, 1426, 1445, 1491, 1503, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

### **Section 4: The Identity and Inheritance of the Peacemakers (Sons of God)**

**Verse**
“ ‘Blessed are the peacemakers, For they shall be called sons of God’ ” (Matthew 5:9). [531, 840, 912, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Paul Washer**—teaches that “blessedness” is the “profound spiritual reality” of finding “repose” in God, and peacemakers are those whose “changed heart is the fruit of regeneration” (Romans 6:17) [11, 24, 114, 142, 282, 1445, Conversation History]. By “pursuing peace with all people,” we prove that we have “received the Spirit of adoption by whom we cry out, ‘Abba, Father’ ” (Hebrews 12:14; Romans 8:15) [8, 13, 211, 212, 285, 435, 525, 1122, 1195, 1197, Conversation History]. To be a “son of God” means being “conformed to the image of His Son,” acting as “ambassador-soldiers” who “contend earnestly for the faith” using the “sword of the Spirit” rather than “carnal weaponry” (Romans 8:29; Jude 3; 2 Corinthians 10:4) [13, 21, 32, 43, 92, 113, 201, 302, 488, 491, 521, 750, 760, 870, 932, 947, 1042, 1081, 1118, 1137, 1141, 1210, 1246, 1313, 1325, 1326, 1334, 1342, 1349, 1357, 1358, 1365, 1367, 1389, 1400, 1402, 1406, 1408, 1410, 1411, 1415, 1426, 1440, 1451, 1453, 1461, 1462, 1463, 1467, 1479, 1503, 1515, 1520, 1601, 1646, 1670, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You must “discipline your body and bring it into subjection,” knowing that “the God of peace will crush Satan under your feet shortly” (1 Corinthians 9:27; Romans 16:20) [12, 13, 79, 101, 116, 551, 875, 959, 1003, 1119, 1228, 1313, 1406, 1408, 1515, 1670, 1709, Conversation History]. “Wait for His Son from heaven,” for the Day is coming when the “Lord Savior” will “judge between the nations,” and His “everlasting dominion” will be the only kingdom that “shall not pass away” (1 Thessalonians 1:10; Isaiah 2:4; Daniel 7:14) [11, 14, 21, 24, 32, 35, 37, 43, 47, 63, 92, 94, 109, 121, 147, 158, 174, 176, 182, 201, 210, 266, 278, 352, 386, 412, 452, 470, 538, 539, 587, 588, 602, 614, 630, 650, 717, 719, 788, 789, 815, 816, 825, 827, 852, 869, 903, 912, 917, 921, 940, 947, 948, 958, 976, 1004, 1035, 1113, 1132, 1143, 1183, 1187, 1189, 1197, 1198, 1211, 1212, 1233, 1241, 1259, 1260, 1266, 1268, 1288, 1290, 1300, 1301, 1306, 1311, 1312, 1313, 1315, 1402, 1408, 1420, 1426, 1450, 1460, 1473, 1502, 1503, 1515, 1519, 1524, 1532, 1572, 1636, 1684, 1720, Conversation History].

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 41, 56, 87, 147, 149, 176, 188, 201, 211, 222, 225, 285, 291, 297, 300, 311, 313, 324, 329, 332, 335, 361, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

references.cited_text: When Christ came into the world, people—especially the disciples—had the opportunity to see God’s character in person. In His High Priestly Prayer, Jesus said to the Father, “I have manifested Your name to the men whom You gave Me” (John 17:6). He didn’t need to tell them about God’s name, but He did need to reveal God’s character to them. John 1:14 tells how that was accomplished: “The Word became flesh, and dwelt among us, and we saw His glory, glory as of the only begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth.” Christ manifested God to the disciples through His own righteous life. That’s why he told Philip, “He who has seen Me has seen the Father” (John 14:9).

Savior’s own commentary on the petition of verse 12—the only petition He provides additional insight into. Obviously the truths here are vitally important: “For if you forgive others for their transgressions, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. But if you do not forgive others, then your Father will not forgive your transgressions.” The first part of the principle is positive: “If you forgive others for their transgressions.” Believers should forgive as those who have received judicial forgiveness from God. When your heart is filled with such a forgiving spirit, “your heavenly Father will also forgive you.” Believers cannot know the parental forgiveness of God, which keeps fellowship with the Lord rich and blessings from Him profuse, apart from forgiving others in heart and word.

God genuinely “desires all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.” Yet, in “the eternal purpose which He carried out in Christ Jesus our Lord” (Eph. 3:11), He chose only the elect “out of the world” (John 17:6) and passed over the rest, leaving them to the damning consequences of their sin (cf. Rom. 1:18–32). The culpability for their damnation rests entirely on them because of their sin and rejection of God. God is not to blame for their unbelief. Since God “desires all men to be saved,” we are not required to ascertain that a person is elect before praying for that person’s salvation. God alone knows who all the elect are (2 Tim. 2:19). We may pray “on behalf of all men” with full assurance that such prayers are “good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior.” After all, “The LORD is gracious and merciful; slow to anger and great in lovingkindness. The LORD is good to all, and His mercies are over all His works” (Ps. 145:8–9).

You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, And you will not be afraid of violence when it comes. You will laugh at violence and famine, And you will not be afraid of wild beasts. That is what justification means. It is the only true gospel. Every other point in the biblical doctrine of salvation emanates from that key truth. As J. I. Packer once wrote, “The doctrine of justification by faith is like Atlas: it bears a world on its shoulders, the entire evangelical knowledge of saving grace.”2 A right understanding of justification by faith is the very foundation of the gospel. Go wrong on this point and you will eventually corrupt every other doctrine as well. What this parable illustrates is the true gospel. All any sinner can possibly do is receive the gift by penitent faith, believing that a perfect atonement must be made—and has been made by Christ—that satisfies the wrath of God against sin. The One who told this story is the One who made the atonement: Jesus Christ. There is no salvation in any other name.

To say it another way: The damned think they are good. The saved know they are wicked. The damned believe the kingdom of God is for those worthy of it. The saved know the kingdom of God is for those who realize how unworthy they are. The damned believe eternal life is earned. The saved know it’s a gift. The damned seek God’s commendation. The saved seek His forgiveness. And He grants forgiveness through the work of Christ. “For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast” (Eph. 2:8–9).

2:14). Now, as His possession, we who were formerly slaves to sin are slaves of a new Lord and Master. Our redemption in Christ results in both freedom from sin and forgiveness for sin. Not only are we liberated from bondage to our former master; we are also exempt from sin’s deadly consequences—namely, the eternal wrath of God. As Paul exclaimed in Romans 8:1–2, “Therefore there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and of death.” Because we are in Him, all of our sins—past, present, and future—have been “forgiven [us] for His name’s sake” (1 John 2:12).24

For you have not received a spirit of slavery [to sin] leading to fear again, but you have received a spirit of adoption as sons by which we cry out, “Abba! Paul could hardly have chosen a better term than ‘adoption’ to characterize this peace and security.”17 Thus Paul’s point in Romans 8:15 is that the spirit of adoption casts out the spirit of fear that comes from slavery to sin.18 The Holy Spirit testifies to our spirits that we are the children of God (v. 16), and if we have the Holy Spirit, we have God’s unbreakable seal guaranteeing our future inheritance.19 Moreover, “adoption does not depend on any worthiness in us, but upon unmerited favor. It is all of grace.”20 We did nothing to earn our adoption into God’s family, and we can do nothing to lose it either.

Believers can therefore be described as those for whom there remains “no condemnation” (Rom. 8:1). They have been sealed with the Holy Spirit, signifying the irrevocable nature of God’s divine guarantee. They are “protected by the power of God” (1 Peter 1:5), such “that He who began a good work in [them] will perfect it until the day of Christ Jesus” (Phil. 1:6). That is why Paul could pray for the Thessalonians, “Now may the God of peace Himself sanctify you entirely; and may your spirit and soul and body be preserved complete, without blame at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. Faithful is He who calls you, and He also will bring it to pass” (1 Thess. 5:23–24; emphasis added). He would echo those same words in his second letter to that same church: “The Lord is faithful, and He will strengthen and protect you from the evil one” (2 Thess. 3:3). Jude similarly concluded his epistle with this triumphant doxology: “Now to Him who is able to keep you from stumbling, and to make you stand in the presence of His glory blameless with great joy, to the only God our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory, majesty, dominion and authority, before all time and now and forever. Amen” (vv. 24–25; emphasis added).
